sourcePolicy: Official ISM monthly reports are authoritative. This file stores a compact analytical snapshot and selected Power Stack-relevant observations, not a reconstructed ISM index database or confidential survey submissions.

manufacturing.powerStackInterpretation: Still strongly supportive of physical-infrastructure demand. Production, orders and backlog accelerated, while customers' inventories fell further into 'too low' territory. The short-supply list continues to include copper, electrical/electronic components, memory and semiconductors. The counterweight is high Prices and slower Supplier Deliveries, which favour suppliers with pricing power and backlog visibility over low-margin contractors.

services.powerStackInterpretation: Demand remains resilient, but inflation is not solved. Business activity and new orders accelerated while employment contracted and Prices returned above 70. Grid, switchgear, transformer, cable and data-centre balance-of-system suppliers retain strong demand support; high fuel, financing and labour costs remain a risk for contractors and transport-intensive businesses.

respondentCommentReview.scope: Only ISM-selected public respondent comments and aggregate diffusion data were reviewed.
respondentCommentReview.conclusion: Selected comments and commodity tables continue to corroborate AI/data-centre procurement, electrical-equipment slot competition, semiconductor/memory demand, defence strength and elevated fuel/freight costs. No evidence today justifies changing the adoption or category hierarchy beyond the existing physical-bottleneck bias.

combinedRead: July ISM remains more bullish for Power Stack physical demand than for a clean disinflation story: manufacturing re-accelerated sharply and services demand stayed firm, but both surveys still show bottlenecks and high prices. The best-positioned exposures remain grid equipment, electrical components, power generation, gas infrastructure and selected automation suppliers with pricing power and backlog visibility.
